question: Should subagent progress extend the existing cross-channel status lifecycle, or should Discord own a separate configurable source-message tracker and shared completion seam?
rationale: Both approaches can produce the requested UX, but the choice establishes permanent configuration, plugin API, lifecycle ownership, and cross-channel precedent that implementation review cannot decide safely.

options.title: Extend the canonical status lifecycle
options.body: Carry prepared subagent count and failure facts into the existing lifecycle controller and let Discord map those facts to native reactions and typing without a parallel owner.

options.title: Sponsor Discord-specific progress
options.body: Accept the separate opt-in tracker and shared completion seam after exact-head proof and explicit compatibility review.

options.title: Defer the feature direction
options.body: Pause or close this PR until maintainers choose a broader subagent progress and liveness model.

recommendation.title: Extend the canonical status lifecycle
recommendation.body: Carry prepared subagent count and failure facts into the existing lifecycle controller and let Discord map those facts to native reactions and typing without a parallel owner.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans both the existing progress/status owner and the shared channel lifecycle API surface needed for this product decision.
